headline: NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) delegation will meet Union ministers at the Constitution Club of India at 12.30 pm on Friday, after the Centre agreed to hold talks at a neutral venueâa key demand raised by the outfit during its ongoing agi...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) delegation will meet Union ministers at the Constitution Club of India at 12.30 pm on Friday, after the Centre agreed to hold talks at a neutral venueâa key demand raised by the outfit during its ongoing agitation over the NEET row.
The meeting comes a day after activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, paving the way for formal discussions between the government and the protesters.
Confirming the development, CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said the organisation welcomed the government's decision to shift the talks to a neutral venue.
"Our protest will continue; Constitution Club of India chosen as venue for meeting with government ministers, hoping for an open-minded dialogue," Das told reporters on Thursday.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
CJP spokesperson Vaishnavi Gaur said the delegation would place the same demands it has been raising since the protests began.
"We will be putting forward our demands, which we have been consistent with from the first day," she said.
According to Gaur, the key demands include the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, compensation for the families affected by the NEET controversy, and withdrawal of all FIRs registered against what she described as "innocent protesters."
'Peaceful protest will continue'Following Wangchuk's decision to end his fast, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke thanked him for what he called an extraordinary act of courage.
"We are relieved and grateful that Sonam sir has ended his hunger strike after 26 days. Thank you for your extraordinary courage and sacrifice. By putting your own life on the line, you awakened the conscience of an entire nation. Your life is far too precious to this country," Dipke wrote in a post on X.
Despite Wangchuk ending his fast, the CJP has maintained that its peaceful protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar will continue until its demands, including Pradhan's resignation, are addressed.

headline: NEW DELHI: BJP Thursday sought to turn the heat on Congress and its allies over the issue of paper leaks as its MPs raised slogans and carried placards in the Parliament complex, targeting Rahul Gandhi and opposition netas for not allowing a discussi...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: BJP Thursday sought to turn the heat on Congress and its allies over the issue of paper leaks as its MPs raised slogans and carried placards in the Parliament complex, targeting Rahul Gandhi and opposition netas for not allowing a discussion on the issue despite govt's willingness to do so.
BJP president Nitin Nabin accused Rahul of running away from debate, asserting that Congress feared that its double-standards would be exposed in Parliament if discussion happened, given that the Opposition had only misled and deceived the youth during its long stint in office.
"I dare them to a debate, but Rahul and his allies will not agree. The NDA govt has shaped the future of the youth in the right direction," he said, highlighting that India is now being recognised for its start-ups and unicorns. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
Congress looks at the youth as nothing but stone-pelters, he said, adding the young population is with PM Modi. Former minister Anurag Thakur asked the Opposition not to play petty politics with students' future. Instead of running away, they should participate in a debate in Parliament, he said, lauding Modi's announcement for setting up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those behind paper leaks. Another party MP, Sudhanshu Trivedi, said BJP and its allies are fully sensitive to the situation.

headline: CJP Nationwide Protest Highlights: 18 Delhi Metro stations continue to remain shut amid CJP protests
full_text:
CJP Nationwide Protest Highlights: 18 Delhi Metro stations continue to remain shut amid CJP protests
Live updates to this blog have ended
Live updates to this blog have ended.
CJP Protest: Additional barricades set up around Jantar Mantar amid Cockroach Janta Party stir, interlinked using chains
Watch: As part of the Delhi Police's crowd-control measures in view of the Cockroach Janta Party's ongoing agitation, additional barricades have been set up around Jantar Mantar, the protest site, and they have been interlinked using heavy-duty chains and reinforced through welding.
#WATCH | Security intensified around Jantar Mantar as Delhi Police set up additional barricades that have been interlinked with heavy duty chains and reinforced through welding. pic.twitter.com/I9tNCvGp6X
— ANI (@ANI) July 25, 2026
(With agency inputs)
CJP Protest: 18 Delhi Metro stations to remain shut today as well, check list
As per the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation's announcement yesterday, 18 stations will remain shut today as well. This comes amid the protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).
The Delhi Metro stations that will remain shut for commuters are:
1. Lok Kalyan Marg
2. Rajiv Chowk
3. Patel Chowk
4. Ramakrishna Ashram Marg
5. Barakhambha Road
6. Supreme Court
7. Seva Teerth
8. Janpath
9. Mandi House
10. Central Secretariat
11. ITO
12. Delhi Gate
13. Indraprastha
14. Khan Market
15. Jor Bagh
16. Shivaji Stadium
17. Jhandewalan
18. New Delhi
While the gates to all the above stations will remain shut, passengers will be able to avail interchange facilities at the Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House and Central Secretariat stations.
Retired civil servants seek judicial probe into police action against protesters
A group of 93 retired civil servants has demanded an independent judicial inquiry into the July 20 police action against student protesters in Delhi, alleging the use of pellet guns, tasers, tear gas and excessive force against demonstrators.
The Constitutional Conduct Group, in a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Delhi Lieutenant Governor V K Saxena and Delhi Police Commissioner, sought action against officers responsible for what it termed "illegal and disproportionate" use of force during and after the 'Sansad Chalo' march.
The signatories, including former Delhi Lieutenant Governor Najeeb Jung, former Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa, former Foreign Secretary Shivshankar Menon, former PMO official A S Dulat, former Punjab DGP Julio Ribeiro and former IAS officer Harsh Mander, alleged that several protesters suffered serious injuries during the police action.
The group claimed that one young protester underwent surgery to remove pellets from her eye and neck, while a 15-year-old child was among those injured and hospitalised.
The retired officials alleged that Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force personnel used pellet guns, electrical batons and tear gas against unarmed protesters. They also accused some personnel, including those without name tags and some in plain clothes, of assaulting demonstrators with lathis, including those allegedly fitted with nails.
The letter further alleged sexual misconduct by at least one policeman and sought identification and strict punishment against the officer.
The group also raised questions over the presence of a truck carrying stones near the protest site, alleged stone-pelting by police personnel, and claimed protesters were detained and moved between police stations without access to lawyers. (Inputs from PTI)
 
Delhi liquor shops to close by 8 PM over the weekend amid student protests
Liquor shops in Delhi will remain open only until 8 pm over the weekend following police inputs on the prevailing situation amid ongoing student protests, sources told PTI on Friday.
An unannounced early closure on Thursday left many customers disappointed as they had to return without alcohol. Liquor shops in the city otherwise remain open until 10 pm.
A senior Delhi government officer said the decision was taken based on police inputs regarding the situation arising from the ongoing protests at Jantar Mantar.
Protests over the NEET issue have intensified in central Delhi over the past few days, with students gathered under the banner of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in the examination process and paper leak allegations. (With inputs from PTI)
 
Youth, lawyers protest in Lucknow; Congress, SP extend support
The agitation over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, particularly the NEET paper leak, spread to Lucknow on Friday as students, youth groups and lawyers staged protests across the city. Demonstrators demanded the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, action against paper leaks and accountability from the government. The Congress held a candlelight march, while the Samajwadi Party extended support through campaigns highlighting its leaders' participation in the Delhi protests. Teacher recruitment aspirants also staged a separate protest over reservation-related demands. (Inputs from PTI)
 
CJP may announce another march to Parliament after today's meeting with government
According to sources, CJP may announce another march to Parliament following its meeting with the government today. (Input from Himanshu Mishra)
CJP Protest Live Updates: Delhi Police sources say Facial Recognition System identified 400 criminals around Jantar Mantar
Delhi Police sources said the Facial Recognition System (FRS) identified around 400 people with criminal records moving in and around the Jantar Mantar protest site between July 20 and July 24. According to the sources, the individuals were detected through the FRS network deployed in the area as part of security arrangements during the ongoing protests.
Aparna Sen backs youth-led CJP protest, slams violence against unarmed students
Veteran filmmaker Aparna Sen has expressed solidarity with students taking part in Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) youth-led protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi, saying they gave her hope and showed her the meaning of democratic dissent.
CJP Protest Live Updates: Delhi metro to close 18 Metro stations tomorrow from 7:30 am
The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has announced that 18 Metro stations will remain closed from 7:30 am on July 25 until further instructions due to the prevailing situation. While entry and exit will remain suspended at these stations, interchange facilities will continue to be available at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House and Central Secretariat.
CJP Protest Live Updates: Third round of Centre-CJP talks likely at 3:30 pm
The third round of talks between Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh and representatives of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) is scheduled to take place at 3:30 pm, according to sources.
Cockroach Janta Party News: Visuals of CJP protest in Pune
CJP Protest Live Updates: Abhijeet Dipke praises Sonam Wangchuk for inspiring nationwide movement
CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke praised Sonam Wangchuk after he ended his fast, saying he had "awakened an entire nation" by risking his own life. In a post on X, Dipke said the country should be grateful to Wangchuk for his sacrifice and contribution to the movement.
CJP Protest Live Updates: Delhi Police debunks reports of food delivery ban in New Delhi
Delhi Police has dismissed as false and misleading social media claims that food delivery app services have been banned across the New Delhi area. In a clarification, the police said no such restriction has been imposed and urged citizens not to share unverified information, advising them to rely only on official sources for authentic updates.
Cockroach Janta Party News: Bhupinder Singh Hooda demands Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
Congress leader Bhupinder Singh Hooda said Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan should resign immediately, holding him responsible for the ongoing crisis. He said the demand was not limited to the Congress or Rahul Gandhi, but reflected the concerns of people across the country, alleging that the future of the youth had been pushed into uncertainty.
CJP Protest Live Updates: Jamia Millia Islamia urges students to stay focused on academics
Jamia Millia Islamia has appealed to students to remain focused on their studies and refrain from participating in any activity that is not in keeping with the law. In a welcome message marking the start of the new academic session, the university said the interests of students would be safeguarded and urged them to act responsibly.
Cockroach Janta Party News: Is this what we pay taxes for? CJP targets PM over Cabinet meet
The Cockroach Janta Party on X handle criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi's advice to Union ministers to become more active on social media, asking, "Is this what we pay our taxes for, so that PM Modi and his ministers can use the Cabinet Meeting to talk about which social media apps to use?" The post added, "Kuch kaam bhi kar lo, we won't have to come on the streets then."
NEET outrage goes national: Protests erupt across states backing Jantar Mantar stir
Protests over the NEET-UG paper leak spread across several states on Friday as students, political activists and civil society groups rallied in support of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) agitation at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, renewing demands for Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and action over the police crackdown on protesters.
CJP Protest Live Updates: Five TVK government ministers to join Tamil Nadu Congress protest
Five ministers from the TVK government are set to participate in the protest organised by the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee against the BJP-led Union government over the alleged NEET paper leak issue.
Cockroach Janta Party News: Gitanjali Angmo urges compassion for Sonam Wangchuk after 26-day fast
Gitanjali J Angmo appealed for compassion towards Sonam Wangchuk, urging people not to criticise him after he ended his 26-day fast. In a post on X, she said Wangchuk was in the ICU after losing 11 kg, including muscle mass, and had "chosen sacrifice over comfort" for a larger cause. She urged people to refrain from judging him, saying the least he deserved was "a day of compassion" before being subjected to political expectations and criticism.

headline: Mamata Banerjee likely to join CJP protest at Jantar Mantar on Monday
full_text:
Mamata Banerjee likely to join CJP protest at Jantar Mantar on Monday
The former West Bengal chief minister had earlier indicated towards joining the protest movement in solidarity with the students.
Trinamool Congress (TMC) chief and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee is likely to join the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest against the alleged NEET paper leak at Jantar Mantar on Monday, people familiar with the matter said.
Banerjee is expected to visit the protest site to express solidarity with the students participating in the agitation, they said.

A senior TMC leader, requesting anonymity, said, “Banerjee will join the CJP’s protest in Delhi on Monday.”
Her participation in what has become one of the largest student-led protests in the national capital is also being seen as an attempt to underline the TMC’s relevance at a time when the party has faced setbacks in both Parliament and the West Bengal assembly.

In a post on X, she wrote: “I have stood firmly with the students and their movement from the very beginning. Their fight is not just for justice in the NEET scam- It is a fight to protect the future of every young Indian. The entire Opposition, along with the entire nation, stands firmly with our students and youth.”

headline: NEW DELHI: BJP leader Pralhad Joshi on Saturday was appointed as the new Union education minister, hours after
full_text:
NEW DELHI: BJP leader Pralhad Joshi on Saturday was appointed as the new Union education minister, hours after 
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned.
Pradhan resigned taking moral responsibility for the NEET-UG paper leak controversy that triggered weeks of nationwide student protests. His resignation was accepted by President Droupadi Murmu.
A press release by Rashtrapati Bhavan read: "The President of India, as advised by the Prime Minister, has accepted the resignation of Shri Dharmendra Pradhan from the Union Council of Ministers, with immediate effect, under clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution of India. Further, as advised by the Prime Minister, the President has directed that Shri Pralhad Joshi, Cabinet Minister, be assigned the charge of the Ministry of Education, in addition to his existing portfolio.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
"
After being appointed as education minister Pralhad Joshi said he accepted the additional charge of the education ministry with 'a sense of duty and humility' and pledged to work under the guidance of PM Modi to further strengthen the country's education system.
"I accept this responsibility with a sense of duty and humility. I am thankful to the Prime Minister. In the last 12 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, many historic achievements have been made. 
In the last four to five years, Dharmendra Pradhan also implemented the National Education Policy, and several important initiatives were undertaken. The country has made significant progress in the new education system. Under the guidance of the Prime Minister, I will work to the best of my ability and fulfil my responsibilities with dedication," Joshi said.
Joshi, the Lok Sabha MP from Karnataka's Dharwad constituency also hold the portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution. A five-time MP, he has previously served as the Union minister for coal, mines and parliamentary affairs.
As the minister for new and renewable energy, Joshi has been leading the Centre's efforts to expand clean energy capacity, with a focus on achieving 500 GW of renewable and non-fossil fuel energy capacity by 2030 and net-zero emissions by 2070.
He has overseen key initiatives including the National Green Hydrogen Mission, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, PM-KUSUM scheme and offshore wind energy projects, while pushing for annual bids for 50 GW of renewable energy capacity and other policy measures to boost the sector.
His appointment comes at a crucial time as the education ministry implements sweeping reforms following the 
NEET-UG controversy, including the restructuring of the National Testing Agency (NTA), stricter anti-paper leak measures and a shift to computer-based testing for NEET from 2027.

headline:
New Delhi: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in Delhi’s Jantar Mantar have triggered a debate on the shifting paradigm in political communication.

Pundits have re...
full_text:
New Delhi: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in Delhi’s Jantar Mantar have triggered a debate on the shifting paradigm in political communication.

Pundits have read it as a rise of the audio-video heavy Instagram as the most effective tool of communication to the masses. Whatapp is a passe, they feel.

The contemporary history of political communication, is replete with examples of how leaders have used social media to amplify their message. Effective communication, does not necessarily depend of the medium or affordance one uses. It’s the message, stupid! And not the messenger.

.Dharmendra Pradhan resignation: Narendra Modi’s first blink gives Opposition a big chance to recoup.

At the 2012 Republican Convention, iconic Hollywood actor director Clint Eastwood launched a 15-minute harangue at empty chair as if it was occupied by the Barak Obama.

President Obama, seeking a second term in office, responded with a terse X (previously Twitter) message that evoked a strong response from his supporters.

It was a picture of a monogrammed chair from the back with Obama sitting. The caption to the post was simple one liner- This seat’s taken.

.

Communication, especially political communication is about messaging- text, visual, audio or a mix of these. Technological interventions simply offer more affordances to the communicators to experiment and reach out to the people.

A good communication strategy is a rational decision making that factors in target audience to create authentic illusions.

Obama was the first world leader to tap into the potential of Twitter to reach out to his support base. And it did work well for him.

Former German Chancellor Angela Merkel instead relied on Instagram. Infact, it is said that she 'Merkelised' Insta to create what pollical scientist Julia Sonnevend and Olivia Steiert call “visually authentic performance.”

In research paper, the two academics, illustrate in some detail how Merkel evolved an image that was in sharp contrast to some of her contemporaries who were using populist rhetoric. The larger leitmotif of Merkel’s Insta posts were driven by “spontaneity, predictability, ordinariness, imperfection, ambivalence, confessions and immediacy.”

For instance, a July 2016 post is a close up of the shoes of Merkel and British PM Theresa May standing at the podium in which May’s bare legs in heels are juxtaposed with Merkel in black pants and slippers.

.

The picture depicts “authenticity and contrast.” And underlines Merkel’s image as a leader know for “rational, evidence-based-decision-making and skilled negotiations.”

Merkel is the not the only leader to make a effective use of Insta for political communication. Former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern posted regularly on Insta to strike a personal connect with the people.

But what worked for Merkel and Jacinda, may or may not work for the others. Every medium has a its own unique grammar. A good screenplay may or may not yield a good film.

Instagram is an audio-visual medium. Its medium where communicators uses pun, context, symbolism, borrows heavily from popular cinema to send across a message. A slight turn of a head, a background score may say lot more than a thousand words.

Moreover, in politics, the focus is now more on individuals around whom political narratives are built. These are personas assiduously evolved over decades in various phases of experimentation and consolidation of the imagery.

In reaching out to a new constituency, there is always the risk of losing the old.

BJP leader LK Advani tried to emulate Vajpayee by travelling to Pakistan after the 2004 defeat of the NDA. That neither helped his personal or his party’s cause.

The picture depicts “authenticity and contrast.” And underlines Merkel’s image as a leader know for “rational, evidence-based-decision-making and skilled negotiations.”

Merkel is the not the only leader to make a effective use of Insta for political communication. Former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern posted regularly on Insta to strike a personal connect with the people.

But what worked for Merkel and Jacinda, may or may not work for the others. Every medium has a its own unique grammar. A good screenplay may or may not yield a good film.

Instagram is an audio-visual medium. Its medium where communicators uses pun, context, symbolism, borrows heavily from popular cinema to send across a message. A slight turn of a head, a background score may say lot more than a thousand words.

Moreover, in politics, the focus is now more on individuals around whom political narratives are built. These are personas assiduously evolved over decades in various phases of experimentation and consolidation of the imagery.

In reaching out to a new constituency, there is always the risk of losing the old.

BJP leader LK Advani tried to emulate Vajpayee by travelling to Pakistan after the 2004 defeat of the NDA. That neither helped his personal or his party’s cause.

headline: BJP veteran MM Joshi says ‘better late than never’ as Pradhan quits; had criticised use of force on CJP protesters
full_text:
BJP veteran MM Joshi says ‘better late than never’ as Pradhan quits; had criticised use of force on CJP protesters
Joshi has not shied away from critiquing Modi regime on policy issues and handling of political controversies, including the Cockroach Janta Party-led protests
A member of the BJP's Margdarshak Mandal (guiding council), the party's former president Murli Manohar Joshi reacted with “better late than never” to Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation amid massive youth protests over exam paper leaks and other issues.
“I appreciate and congratulate all the students for their peaceful conclusion to the movement. I hope that now peace will soon be established in the world of Indian education and that the young people will have ample opportunities for their bright future and progress,” said Joshi, who also led India's education policy as minister in Atal Bihari Vajpayee's BJP-led NDA government nearly three decades ago.
He also said he hoped the PM “will take an immediate and timely decision”, purportedly referring to a nod to the resignation.
Veteran who speaks up
MM Joshi, 92, and former deputy PM LK Advani, 98, are on the Margdarshak Mandal of the BJP as they were deemed too advanced in age for active ministerial work when Modi became PM in 2014.
The BJP website lists PM Modi himself, 75, and defence minister Rajnath Singh, 75, as other members of the council, as of July 25.
Joshi headed the education ministry between 1998 and 2004 and at the time, faced criticism for changing the curriculum and history textbooks for alleged “saffronisation”.
Joshi has not shied away from critiquing the Modi regime on policy issues and handling of political controversies, including the Cockroach Janta Party-led protests now. In an earlier post on X, Joshi expressed deep anguish at the use of force against the demonstrators during the ongoing protests and cautioned that this would alienate large sections from the national goal of Viksit Bharat (developed India).
“It is deeply painful to see that young students from different parts of the country have been gathered on the streets of New Delhi for several days. Their concerns and issues are genuine. These must be addressed with empathy and a vision for long-term solutions. I sincerely hope this will not be viewed merely as a law-and-order problem to be dealt with by force,” he said in a post on X.
On July 20, the Delhi Police used force to stop a march by thousands of demonstrators towards Parliament. Videos that surfaced on social media showed several protesters, many of them appearing unarmed, being beaten by police personnel in riot gear, with some sustaining head injuries. Police, however, maintained that the crowd had turned violent, necessitating the use of force.
But the protest grew from that moment and concluded on Saturday as the minister resigned.

headline: All about Pralhad Joshi: BJP's 'blue-eyed boy' now in charge of education ministry after Pradhan quits
full_text:
All about Pralhad Joshi: BJP's 'blue-eyed boy' now in charge of education ministry after Pradhan quits
Pralhad Venkatesh Joshi is currently the Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, as well as New and Renewable Energy.
After President Droupadi Murmu on Saturday accepted the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as education minister, senior BJP leader Pralhad Joshi has been given the additional charge of the Education Ministry.
The development came just hours after Pradhan announced that he had submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Who is Pralhad Joshi?
Pralhad Venkatesh Joshi is currently the Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, as well as New and Renewable Energy. Along with these portfolios, he will now also oversee the Education Ministry.

Joshi returned to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Cabinet in 2024. A five-time Member of Parliament, he is regarded as one of the BJP's trusted leaders and is often described as the "blue-eyed boy" of the party's top leadership.
Political journey
Born in November 1962 into a traditional North Karnataka Brahmin family, Joshi entered national politics after being elected to the 14th Lok Sabha in 2004.
Also read | Pralhad Joshi gets education ministry charge as Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation accepted
He became associated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) at a young age and later rose through the ranks of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
His electoral journey began in 1996 when he was elected to the Karnataka Legislative Assembly. Eight years later, he entered Parliament after winning the Dharwad-Hubballi Lok Sabha seat in 2004. Since then, he has retained the constituency in every general election, securing victories in 2009, 2014, 2019 and 2024.
Rise within the BJP
Joshi's active participation in parliamentary debates, particularly on development, infrastructure and education, strengthened his position within the BJP. His growing influence earned him the reputation of being one of the party high command's most trusted leaders.
In 2019, he joined Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Cabinet as Union Minister for Parliamentary Affairs, Coal and Mines. He returned to the Union Cabinet in 2024.
Faced challenge in 2024 Lok Sabha election
Despite his strong political standing, Joshi's latest electoral battle was not without hurdles. He faced opposition from sections of the influential Lingayat community in Karnataka, with Lingadishwar seer emerging as a key challenger through his followers.
Dispute resolved before election
The differences were eventually resolved with the intervention of senior leaders, including former chief minister BS Yediyurappa.
Dharwad city BJP block president Tippana Majjagi said the misunderstanding between the two sides had been settled.
A key face in Karnataka BJP
Over the years, Joshi has remained one of the BJP's most prominent leaders from Karnataka. Despite political challenges and criticism, he has continued to retain his electoral base and remains an influential figure within both the state unit and the party's national leadership.

headline: Sarnath becomes India's 45th Unesco World Heritage Site, PM calls it a proud moment
full_text:
Sarnath becomes India's 45th Unesco World Heritage Site, PM calls it a proud moment
The ancient Buddhist site Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh has been inscribed on the Unesco World Heritage List, becoming India's 45th World Heritage Site during the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea.
India's ancient Buddhist site of Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh was on Saturday inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List during the 48th session of the Unesco World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea.
Unesco announced the decision in a post on X, saying, "New inscription on the Unesco World Heritage List: Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath, India."
The inscription makes Sarnath India's 45th site on the Unesco World Heritage List.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the recognition and described it as "a proud moment for every Indian."
"A proud moment for every Indian! Delighted that Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh has been inscribed on the Unesco World Heritage List," PM Modi said in a post on X.
The Prime Minister said Sarnath has a deep connection with Lord Buddha, whose timeless message of wisdom, compassion and harmony continues to inspire the world.
"This recognition celebrates India's profound civilisational and spiritual heritage. It will also inspire more people across the world to come to Sarnath and connect with the ideals of Lord Buddha," he said.
Located around 10 kilometres from Varanasi, Sarnath is one of the most significant pilgrimage sites for Buddhists across the world. It holds a unique place in history as the site where Gautam Buddha delivered his first sermon.
The decision to inscribe Sarnath on the World Heritage List was taken during the ongoing 48th session of the Unesco World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea.
In August 2025, Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat informed the Lok Sabha in a written reply that India had submitted a dossier titled "Ancient Buddhist Site, Sarnath" to the Unesco World Heritage Centre for the 2025-26 nomination cycle.
The World Heritage Committee is one of the two bodies that govern the Convention for the Protection of the World's Cultural and Natural Heritage.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah also welcomed the development, saying, "Our cultural pride soars even higher today as Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh has been included in the Unesco World Heritage List."
Calling it an endorsement of India's ancient heritage associated with Lord Buddha, Shah said the recognition would take the Buddha's luminous wisdom to more people and inspire them to embrace the ideals of peace and enlightenment for a better world.
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India's timeless civilisational heritage continues to receive global recognition.
"Sarnath's inscription on the Unesco World Heritage List is a proud moment for every Indian and a shining reflection of Uttar Pradesh's glorious spiritual and cultural legacy," he said, adding that Uttar Pradesh welcomes the world to experience this eternal heritage.

headline: NEW DELHI: Saturday witnessed a series of major developments in the NEET paper leak controversy, beginning with Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation after weeks of nationwide protests.
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Saturday witnessed a series of major developments in the NEET paper leak controversy, beginning with Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation after weeks of nationwide protests. 
Hours later, Pralhad Joshi was appointed as the new education minister getting additional charge apart from portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution. 
Meanwhile, the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party (
CJP) held a third round of talks, after which the government agreed to withdraw FIRs filed against peaceful protesters. 
Following the meeting, the CJP announced the immediate withdrawal of its 36-day agitation at Jantar Mantar, saying it was ending the protest in "good faith" after the government accepted its key demands. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
The protest site was cleared after the CJP demands were met. 
The developments marked the biggest political fallout of the NEET controversy, which triggered nationwide student protests, a CBI probe and sweeping reforms to India's examination system.
Here are the top developments:Pralhad Joshi gets additional charge of education ministry
Hours after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, President Droupadi Murmu assigned senior BJP leader Pralhad Joshi the additional charge of the Union education ministry on the advice of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. 
A five-time Lok Sabha MP from Karnataka's Dharwad, Joshi will continue to hold the portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution. He takes charge at a crucial time as the government rolls out reforms following the NEET-UG paper leak, including restructuring the NTA, tightening exam security and shifting NEET to computer-based testing from 2027.
After being given the charge, Joshi said: "The Prime Minister has placed his trust in me and has entrusted me with such a significant responsibility. With complete humility and a strong sense of responsibility, I will fulfil this duty...I thank the Prime Minister for giving me this important responsibility and for showing such great confidence in me. Under his guidance and leadership, I will work sincerely and try my best to meet his expectations in this department. With full dedication, humility, and honesty, I will work towards fulfilling this responsibility. I once again thank the Prime Minister for giving me this opportunity."
Metro stations reopen after protest ends
Normal Metro access resumed across Delhi after the CJP called off its 36-day protest, with the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) reopening the entry gates of all stations that had been closed because of security arrangements.
The reopening came shortly after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and the Centre reached an agreement with the CJP to end the agitation. 
Earlier in the day, the DMRC had resumed services at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House and Central Secretariat stations before restoring entry and exit at all 18 affected stations, which had been placed under restrictions due to the protests near Jantar Mantar.
 Pradhan resigns, cites moral responsibility
Announcing his resignation in a letter addressed to the country's youth, Pradhan said he had submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi after considering the situation that had developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country.
He said he had spent more than four decades working for students, teachers and education reforms and had always believed that a strong education system was the foundation of a strong nation. Pradhan said the government acted immediately after irregularities surfaced in the NEET-UG examination by handing the investigation to the CBI, cancelling the examination and announcing a fresh test, while also deciding to shift NEET to computer-based mode from next year.
He added that he had accepted responsibility from the very beginning and had worked to ensure that no deserving student suffered because of what he described as an examination mafia. 
Recalling the events of the past few days had deeply saddened him, Pradhan said he was stepping down to prevent anti-national forces from exploiting the situation, safeguard national unity and allow students to focus on their education.
 Centre and CJP reach agreement after third round of talks
Hours after Pradhan's resignation, the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party held a third round of talks, following which the student group announced the immediate withdrawal of its 36-day protest.
Addressing a joint press conference with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, CJP spokespersons Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das said the agitation was being withdrawn in good faith after the government accepted its key demands.
The CJP said its primary demand, Pradhan's resignation, had been fulfilled. It also said the Centre had agreed to withdraw FIRs and legal cases against peaceful protesters and assured that no retaliatory action would be taken.
  The government further agreed to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide in accordance with existing rules and regulations and promised to consider the CJP's five-point charter on examination reforms.
JP Nadda said the government had sympathetically considered the delegation's demands and would hold further discussions on long-term reforms to strengthen the examination system.
Student movement ends after 36 days
The CJP protest began at Jantar Mantar on June 20, demanding accountability over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak, wider reforms in the examination system and Pradhan's resignation.
 The movement gained national attention after climate activist 
Sonam Wangchuk joined the agitation with an indefinite hunger strike. His deteriorating health and later hospitalisation intensified public attention and increased pressure on the government.
Although Wangchuk ended his 26-day fast after receiving written assurances from the Centre, the CJP continued its protest until Pradhan resigned and the remaining demands were addressed.
Speaking after the agreement, Ashutosh Ranka appealed to protesters across the country to withdraw peacefully, while Saurav Das said the movement was ending with the understanding that all commitments would be implemented within the agreed timelines.
"Government accepted all our demands after 36 days of protest; we urge everyone to peacefully withdraw from protest sites," CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said.
Earlier in the day, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had briefly said the protest would continue until all demands were accepted. After the talks concluded, however, the organisation announced the end of the agitation.
Dipke also urged supporters not to treat Pradhan's resignation as a personal victory for him, saying the movement was driven by thousands of young people and should remain focused on institutional reforms rather than individuals.
Amit Shah reacts to Pradhan's exit
Union home minister Amit Shah reacted to Dharmendra Pradhan's exit as education minister saying, "Modi government respects youth's sentiments". 
"For BJP workers, the country, our youth, and students are far more important than any position. Today, the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan ji from his post exemplifies this very principle. The Modi government respects the sentiments of the country's youth and is committed to implementing the necessary reforms against paper leaks. The decisions taken by Modi ji to ensure strict punishment for those guilty of paper leaks are commendable. I am fully confident that these steps will ensure complete justice for the students who succeeded in the NEET examination.," he said.
"During his tenure, Shri Dharmendra Pradhan ji has brought about significant reforms in the effective implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP), arrangements for examinations in mother tongues, expansion of PM SHRI Schools, promotion of digital education, skill development, and strengthening industry-academia coordination. His efforts toward making the examination system more inclusive and student-centric have also been noteworthy. His tenure is a testament to his dedication to the resolve of making India a developed nation," he added.
Opposition calls it a victory for students
The opposition described Pradhan's resignation as a major victory for students and renewed calls for broader reforms in the education system.
Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi called the resignation "the victory of the future of India", saying Pradhan had become a symbol of corruption, incompetence and the decline of the country's education system. 
He said the government must now introduce meaningful reforms and alleged that the issue of police action against student protesters would remain a key matter during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge termed the resignation a "victory of truth" and said Prime Minister Narendra Modi should apologise to the country's youth while ensuring action against those responsible for the alleged use of force against protesters.
AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal described the development as a "big win for democracy", while Karnataka chief minister DK 
Shivakumar said the Congress would continue raising issues concerning students and maintained that peaceful protests were an essential part of democracy.
Wangchuk welcomes outcome
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk welcomed the developments, describing them as "a victory of democracy, direct democracy, peace, patience and perseverance". He congratulated the student movement and thanked citizens across the country for supporting the agitation.
His wife, Gitanjali Angmo, also praised the role played by India's younger generation, saying the protests had demonstrated courage, patriotism and commitment to democratic values without violence.
Tougher anti-paper leak law proposed
The Centre has proposed major amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act to ensure faster investigations, time-bound trials and stricter punishment for paper leaks and examination malpractice.
The proposed Bill provides for the creation of Special Task Forces (STFs) to investigate offences, completion of investigations within two months, day-to-day hearings in special fast-track courts and disposal of appeals by High Courts within three months.
It also significantly increases penalties, proposing jail terms of up to 10 years and fines of up to Rs 10 crore for organised paper leak rackets, along with tougher action against service providers and officials found involved in examination fraud.
Biggest political fallout of NEET controversy
Pradhan's resignation marks the most significant political consequence of the NEET-UG paper leak controversy, which began after allegations of question paper leaks in the May 3 examination.
The controversy led to the cancellation of the examination, a nationwide CBI investigation, repeated protests, parliamentary disruptions, changes to the anti-paper leak law and a major restructuring of the National Testing Agency.
Pradhan also removed education minister from his X bio following the resignation.

headline: Dharmendra Pradhan resigns as education minister amid massive paper leak protests
full_text:
Dharmendra Pradhan resigns as education minister amid massive paper leak protests
Dharmendra Pradhan said that he was taking the decision to resign keeping the future and career of students in mind. He has sent his resignation to PM Modi.
Education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday, after weeks of massive student protests in Delhi seeking his resignation over exam irregularities, particularly the NEET-UG paper leak.
Pradhan announced his resignation from the post on X. He said that he was taking the decision keeping the future of students in mind. "...To ensure that anti-national elements are not benefitted by the situation at Jantar Mantar and across the country, that the nation remains united, students in India do not get tangled in legal complexities and focus on their studies and their career, I have tendered my resignation to the Prime Minister...," the letter reads. Follow live updates on the CJP protest here.
The development comes a day after spokespersons from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the Abhijeet Dipke-led outfit that has been leading the protests, met union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh.
After the meeting, the CJP had said that the government had sought day's time to decide on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.
Read Dharmendra Pradhan's full letter here (Translated from Hindi).
My young friends,
I have been dedicated to students, teachers, and education reform for over four decades. It has always been my firm belief that a strong, inclusive, and visionary education system is the foundation of a strong nation.
I deeply respect the aspirations, emotions, and legitimate expectations of the country's youth. Fulfilling the dreams of India's young generation has been a moral commitment in all of our political and social lives. I express my gratitude to the Honorable Prime Minister for giving me the opportunity to serve the nation under his visionary leadership.
However, irregularities were found in the NEET-UG examination held on May 3, 2026. Taking immediate cognizance, the Government of India handed over the investigation to the CBI, cancelled the exam, and announced a re-examination date. Along with this, it was decided to conduct this exam in CBT (Computer-based-test) mode starting next year.
During this period, our primary priority was to ensure that the exam for over 20 lakh students was conducted smoothly. For this, work was carried out under a "whole of government approach." In this, along with the Government of India, state governments and particularly district administrations played a crucial role. Furthermore, with the cooperation of students, guardians, and parents, this examination was completed on June 21, 2026.
From day one, I took responsibility for this and never turned away from the situation. It was my resolve that we would not allow the future of any meritorious student to be ruined by the exam mafia, nor would we allow injustice to happen to any student.
The NEET-UG results declared on July 16 were satisfactory, in which many meritorious students from underprivileged backgrounds also achieved success.
However, even during this time, people sitting in responsible positions attempted to create hurdles and mislead many students, which deeply distressed my mind.
I have always been someone with unwavering faith in the strength of our democracy, and I have always deeply respected the aspirations, dreams, and expectations of the youth. They are not just the future of India, but also the carriers, builders, and architects of a new and developed India.
Looking at the developments over the last 10 days, my heart is deeply saddened. This is not a matter of personal prestige for me.
The youth power of India is the true strength of this country.
We will not let the country's youth power fall into a web of confusion—this is my resolve.
Considering that anti-national forces should not take advantage of the situation that has arisen at Jantar Mantar and across the country, that the unity of the nation remains intact, that the future of even a single student in India does not get entangled in legal complexities, and that our children invest their time in studying and focus on building their careers—considering all of this, I have sent my resignation to the Honorable Prime Minister.
I express my heartfelt gratitude to the Honorable Prime Minister for his guidance, trust, and continuous support. At the same time, I also express my gratitude to all my respected colleagues in the Council of Ministers, officials and employees of the ministry, and all those individuals with whom I had the privilege to work. Service to the nation is the highest priority of my life. I will always remain dedicated to it.
With the blessings of Lord Shree Jagannath Ji, I will continue to dedicate myself in every possible way in the future to fulfill the aspirations of Mother India, the people of Odisha, and the youth of the country.
Yours,
Dharmendra Pradhan
CJP welcomes move, celebrations at Jantar Mantar
The CJP, which had long been seeking Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, welcomed the union minister's announcement. “The Education Minister has submitted his resignation. Chhatra Shakti Zindabad (Long live Student Power)!”
During a media interaction, Dipke later said: "Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned. And this resignation is proof that if you people are not afraid, if you people do not bow down to this government, then we can take the resignation of anyone."
Shortly after Pradhan's announcement, the CJP shared a video on Instagram, showing people at Jantar Mantar celebrating and Dipke sitting on his knees and on his phone.
The CJP began its protest in Delhi last month and the students' support to the agitation only grew ever since climate activist Sonam Wangchuk began his hunger strike. Despite Wangchuk calling off his fast this week, the CJP stayed firm on Pradhan's resignation demand, making it clear that “nothing lesser” would be acceptable.
Agreement on 2 demands ‘in-principle’
The CJP had three key demands - Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, compensation for family of students who died by suicide, and assurance of no legal action against protesters.
After the second CJP-government meeting on Friday, Dipke's party had said that the government had “in-principle” approved two of three demands and would decide on Pradhan's resignation later.
Roughly 24 hours later, Pradhan has resigned.
The NEET-UG 2026 exam took place on May 3, but the government announced its cancellation on May 12, citing a paper leak. The decision triggered massive uproar and the backlash only grew after several aspirants died by suicide. A re-exam took place on June 21 and results were announced this month.

headline: Around 2.25 pm, as soon as the news of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation broke, Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement, shouted jubilantly.
full_text:
Around 2.25 pm, as soon as the news of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation broke, Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement, shouted jubilantly.
Jantar Mantar protest updates on July 25, 2026
He then grabbed a microphone, walked to the front of the stage and addressed the thousands gathered at Jantar Mantar protest site: “We have done it.”
With his fists closed and raised in the air, he declared, “Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned. It was said that resignations do not happen in this government. Even the world will bow if there is a person to make it happen.”
The protest site erupted in celebration. Protesters hugged one another, broke into tears, and danced to patriotic Bollywood songs as chants of victory echoed through the crowd and slogans like “Haar gaye, haar gaye, Tanashah haar gaye [dictator has been defeated]” reverberated across the venue.
For many students who had spent days braving rain, heat, and sleeping on roads while demanding accountability, the announcement was more than a political development. It was an emotional affirmation that their voices had finally been heard.
Despite the resignation, which was one of the major demands, the crowd at Jantar Mantar continued to swell as people wanted to celebrate the “historic victory”.
Dozens gathered in front of the main stage to take selfies, while long queues were seen outside the entrance of the venue as thousands of people continued to stream in to the protest site.
Inside the protest site, slogans of “Inquilab Zindabad” and “Bharat Mata ki Jai” filled the air. Some also chanted “Jang abhi bhi jaari hai, E20 ki baari hai” (the fight is not over, E20 is the next target) even as organisers repeatedly appealed to the gathering to maintain peace.
As A.R. Rahman’s ‘Vande Matram’ played from the stage, people sang along, as Mr. Dipke waved the national flag from the centre of the stage. People continued to celebrate as “Chak De! India” blared from the stage.
People distributed “Melody” chocolate in celebration, an apparent reference to Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifting the confectionery to the Italian Prime Minister earlier this year. Mr. Dipke, who had been unwell, soon left the area.
At around 6 p.m., CJP spokespersons Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das returned after meeting Union Ministers and announced that “we have won”, triggering another round of applause.
About half an hour later, Mr. Ranka urged people to disperse peacefully as the protest had been called off. “We will meet you soon,” he said, as both of them left the area.
While many people started to leave, hundreds continued to pour in to celebrate, forcing the volunteers to close the entries to the protest site. Thousands of people who were still coming to the protest site gathered at the Sansad Marg leading to Connaught Place.
By 8:30 pm, workers had started to dismantle the main stage. But, still people climbed on it to click selfies, amid chants of “Vande Bharatam” and fluttering of national flags.
Protesters divided
However, not all protesters agreed with the decision to call off the agitation.
Kuldeepak Yadav, 29, from Firozabad, Uttar Pradesh, who said he had been at the protest site since it began, was of the opinion that it would have been difficult to continue the protest after the government had agreed to the three core demands. “If we continue the protest, a lot of people who are originally associated with the movement may distance themselves,” he said.
But Vrutika, 17, from Mumbai, who had joined the protest a day earlier with her father, had a different take. “The protest should continue seeking the Prime Minister’s resignation. There are many pressing issues, such as price rise, financial distress, and lack of regard for the Constitution,” the Class XII student said.
“I came here to fight for education and also my rights,” she added.

headline: Longest mobile internet shutdown in Delhi's history eases as CJP withdraws protest
full_text:
Longest mobile internet shutdown in Delhi's history eases as CJP withdraws protest
With the seventh extension that came on Saturday, mobile internet in the area remained repeatedly suspended for five days.
Delhi witnessed its longest internet shutdown during the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest demanding the resignation of (now former) education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. On Saturday morning, the government issued a seventh order extending the suspension of mobile internet services around Jantar Mantar until 12 midnight.
However, people in and around the affected area said mobile internet services were restored shortly after Pradhan announced his resignation on X and the CJP called off its protest, saying the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government had agreed to its demands.
The restoration came well before the scheduled midnight deadline for the suspension. Despite the restoration, telecom service providers (TSPs) had not received any formal order revoking the suspension until late Saturday evening, said people aware of the matter.
In the last five days, it was only on July 21 when the government did not issue a suspension order. With the seventh extension that came Saturday, mobile internet in the area remained repeatedly suspended for five days, making it the longest such disruption recorded in the national capital.
Also Read | Jantar Mantar protest: Delhi Police FIR includes charge of attempt to murder
A timeline of shutdowns
The shutdown began on July 20, when the government directed TSPs, including Airtel, Reliance Jio and Vodafone Idea, to suspend mobile internet services from 10 am to 6 pm in parts of central Delhi around Jantar Mantar. A second order followed on July 22, directing operators to suspend services from 6 pm until 6 am the next morning.
On July 23, the government first extended the suspension from 9.30 am to 4.30 pm before issuing another order extending it until midnight. On Friday, authorities again suspended mobile internet until noon before issuing a sixth order extending the shutdown till 12 midnight. On Saturday, a seventh order further extended the suspension till 12 midnight.
The orders require telecom companies to suspend mobile internet services within a 1.5-km radius of the protest site. Affected areas include Janpath Market near Connaught Place, Le Meridien, Shangri-La hotel, the National Media Centre and the Indian Women’s Press Corps office.
Digital rights organisation SFLC.in also challenged the internet shutdown orders before the Delhi High Court, arguing that the suspension of mobile internet services in parts of central Delhi during the July 2026 protests was unlawful.
A history of shutdowns
While Delhi has seen internet shutdowns before, they have been shorter and linked to specific law-and-order situations.
One such instance was in December 2019, during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), when mobile internet services were suspended for several hours in parts of the capital. The shutdown was ordered by Delhi Police, which is empowered to direct telecom operators to suspend services under the temporary telecom suspension rules.
Another instance of internet shutdown occurred during the farmers’ protests in 2021. In January 2021, the government suspended mobile internet services in adjoining areas of Delhi. The suspension was later extended at some of the Delhi border protest sites, including Singhu, Ghazipur and Tikri, as the farmers’ agitation continued.
Unlike the 2019 and 2021 disruptions, the current shutdown was extended through multiple consecutive government orders over several days.
The repeated internet suspensions pushed protesters to look for alternative ways to communicate. Some turned to apps such as Bitchat Mesh, which do not depend on mobile internet. Instead, the app creates a Bluetooth-based mesh network that connects nearby users, allowing messages to be exchanged without an internet connection.
The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the Home Ministry, also issued a notice to GitHub under section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act, directing it to remove URLs hosting BitChat, said the messaging app’s founder Jack Dorsey on X on Friday.

Wangchuk responds to criticism

Dharmendra Pradhan resigns LIVE: CJP says Pradhan resignation ‘just a trailer’
After the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) withdrew its protest from Jantar Mantar, spokesperson Saurav Das on Saturday said that the outfit will continue to raise the youth's issues.
Meanwhile, the CJP has withdrawn their agitation, saying the decision was taken in "good faith" as the government agreed to its demands. Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as the education minister following over a month-long protest across the nation.
Das told reporters, "Democracy has been restored. Democracies demand accountability, answerability. The youth of the country are the future; they have been able to restore it. Speaking to reporters in Ahilyanagar, the 89-year-old activist recalled his own history of civil agitation to emphasise that lasting systemic change comes through conversation rather than confrontation.

"Any issue gets resolved through dialogue. Dialogue leads to solutions. Creating tension and going down the wrong path will not solve anything. Dialogue is the most crucial thing. In a statement, Fadnavis credited Pradhan with leading key reforms in the education sector, including the implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP), the launch of PM SHRI Schools, expansion of IITs abroad and conducting national entrance examinations in 19 languages.
"Shri Dharmendra Pradhan ji has undertaken several important reforms in the country's education sector. He played a pivotal role in implementing the National Education Policy," Fadnavis said.
Referring to Pradhan's resignation, which came after the nationwide protests spearheaded by the Cockroach Janta Party over the NEET paper leak scandal, the chief minister said it reflected his commitment to the larger good of society.
"By submitting his resignation today, he has once again demonstrated that for a BJP worker, the nation always comes first. He placed the nation's interest above personal gain, which is the hallmark of a true BJP karyakarta (volunteer)," Fadnavis said.

Dharmendra Pradhan resigns LIVE: BJP veteran MM Joshi says ‘better late than never’ as Pradhan quits

“I appreciate and congratulate all the students for their peaceful conclusion to the movement. He also said he hoped the PM “will take an immediate and timely decision”, purportedly referring to formal acceptance of the resigantion.

Stephane Dujarric, Spokesman for Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, responding to a question on Friday about the UN's position on the youth-led protests in India, said, "We're obviously very much aware of the protests that we've seen in New Delhi."
"It is important that people wishing to protest peacefully be allowed to do so without the fear of harassment, the fear of arrest, or the fear of injury," said Dujarric.
Dharmendra Pradhan resigns LIVE: Pradhan's exit joins short list of Modi govt's climbdowns since 2014
Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation on Saturday over the NEET paper leak controversy was not the sole instance when the Narendra Modi government yielded to sustained public or political pressure since coming to power in 2014.
The first major retreat came in 2015 when the government sought to amend the land acquisition law to make it easier to acquire land for infrastructure and industrial projects.
The move triggered widespread opposition from farmer organisations, opposition parties and several NDA allies, who argued that the changes diluted existing safeguards and were anti-people. The government eventually allowed the proposal to lapse. Modi announced that the existing law would remain unchanged.
Three years later came the first ministerial resignation under public pressure.
In October 2018, then minister of state for external affairs M J Akbar resigned during the Me Too movement after several women accused him of sexual harassment during his days as an editor. Akbar denied the allegations but stepped down.
The government's biggest policy reversal came in November 2021 when Modi announced the repeal of the three farm laws.
The laws triggered a yearlong agitation, with thousands of farmers camping at Delhi's borders demanding their withdrawal. Although the government consistently defended the reforms, it eventually gave in, with Parliament passing the repeal legislation.
In August 2024, the Centre withdrew a UPSC advertisement for lateral recruitment to senior civil services after objections from opposition parties and NDA ally Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) over the absence of reservation provisions.
Another retreat followed in November 2025 when the government decided against introducing the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill after facing strong political opposition, particularly from parties in Punjab, which argued that the proposal would dilute the state's political representation.
Pradhan's resignation on Saturday marks the latest instance of the government conceding to pressure.

headline: ‘Police are everywhere’: Sonam Wangchuk's wife questions heavy deployment at Medanta
full_text:
‘Police are everywhere’: Sonam Wangchuk's wife questions heavy deployment at Medanta
Angmo's post comes after Wangchuk shared a video late Friday night questioning whether he needed a “character certificate” after 26 days of hunger strike.
Scientist and activist Sonam Wangchuk's wife Gitanjali Angmo questioned the heavy deployment of police in the hospital where he is admitting, claiming that the authorities are deciding who “may or may not meet him”.
Angmo shared a picture from the hospital on Saturday showing several police officers standing in the lobby of Medanta Hospital in Gurugram where Wangchuk is currently admitted after Delhi high court's order.
He was earlier taken to Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital by Delhi police amid his hunger strike in support of students demanding education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. This fast was broken late Thursday night when Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh visited him at the hospital to convey the government's decision to concede to some of his demands.
Also Read I 'Have a heart': Sonam Wangchuk's wife urges people to not judge him for breaking 26-day fast
‘Police are everywhere’
In the post shared by Angmo, she questioned the heavy deployment of police at Medanta Hospital and said that “police are everywhere”.
“At both Safdarjung and now Medanta, police are everywhere. At the main gate. The reception. The lifts. Outside @Wangchuk66’s ICU. They decide who may or may not meet him. If the Court has clarified that he is not under detention, then under what authority is this happening?” she questioned.
“In an enlightened democracy, is the role of the police to protect citizens and uphold the law, or to control citizens on behalf of those in power? These are questions every Indian should be asking,” she added.
The official Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) handle also drew attention to Angmo's post.
Angmo's post comes after Wangchuk also shared a video late Friday night questioning whether he still needed a “character certificate” after 26 days of hunger strike, following allegations of a “deal” with the government.
In a 22-minute long tell-all video posted on his YouTube handle, Wangchuk alleged ill-treatment via police occupation at Safdarjung Hospital and refusal to let him go after a High Court order granted him permission to shift to a private facility of his choice.
Also Read I 'Govt sought time till tomorrow on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation demand': CJP after second meeting
A clip in the video showed Wangchuk trying to get away from Safdarjung Hospital but being denied exit by cops positioned on the hospital floor. The confrontation turned aggressive as Wangchuk lay on the ground, refusing to move from the spot.
“Arrest me. Why are you forcing... people, this is torture. Now arrest me if you want, you understand? Arrest me, arrest me. You can stop me wherever, let the nation know how,” he can be heard saying angrily in the video taken and uploaded by an aide from his team as cops try to chase him down the hospital corridor.
“It is digitally everywhere. The world knows except you. The world knows,” he says in reference to the Delhi High Court order allowing him to be transferred to Medanta Hospital.
In his YouTube video, Wangchuk also addressed questions regarding why he dropped education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as well as the manner in which he broke his fast by saying that he feared a violent government crackdown similar to the one seen in Ladakh during his last hunger strike. He emphasised that his priorities in this instance were to ensure legal impunity for all students who are protesting peacefully.
Police, hospital authorities clarify
Officials have clarified that the video was recorded at Safdarjung Hospital on July 21, the day of the High Court order. "This is from July 21 July, the day when the court informed Sonam's family that he can be moved to Medanta hospital," an official said.
“He was trying to leave for Medanta hospital, but was not allowed, as we were waiting for the court orders to come to us first and hence we were stopping him,” the official clarified as the reason for attempts to block Wangchuk's exit.
Safdarjung Hospital cited a similar reason by stating that all preparations were in place to handover Wangchuk to the medical team at Medanta Hospital as soon as the High Court order officially reached them.
"The video was reportedly recorded before the hospital administration received the written order of the high court. At that time, Mr Wangchuk insisted on leaving the hospital based on information available in the media," the hospital's statement said, as per PTI report.
“It is pertinent to note that Mr Wangchuk was handed over to the team of doctors from Medanta Gurugram on the same day at 6:40 pm, immediately after the written order was received by the hospital."
Currently, Wangchuk is under recovery at Medanta Hospital. The CJP has vowed to continue its nationwide protests until Pradhan's resignation. Representatives from the party are scheduled to have another round of talks with Nadda and Singh in the afternoon. Track CJP protest LIVE updates here

headline: Opposition parties on Saturday (July 25, 2026) termed the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, following widespread student protests over the NEET paper leak, a “victory for the youth” and a step towards rebuilding the country’...
full_text:
Opposition parties on Saturday (July 25, 2026) termed the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, following widespread student protests over the NEET paper leak, a “victory for the youth” and a step towards rebuilding the country’s education system.
Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi urged other groups to show courage like the students and stand up against the government. “It is time to remove the government,” he said.
“Symbolic but big step”
He said Mr. Pradhan’s resignation was a significant step towards rebuilding the education system. “It’s a symbolic step because he was a symbol, but it is still a big step,” he said.
The Congress leader also said the resignation is a signal to other communities, including farmers, labourers, and the poor, who are allegedly being oppressed by the government. “There is wisdom and courage in standing up. “Daro mat [don’t be afraid]. Let’s get rid of this regime that is attacking India, destroying our Constitution and capturing all our institutions,” Mr. Gandhi said in a video message posted on X and later, while speaking to the media.
Congress MP from Wayanad Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said this was the day when the people started “claiming their country back”. “The youth did not bend; the government had to bend. It is a victory for the youth and students of India. I was truly happy when I heard the news. I even got a bit emotional,” she told the media in her constituency. “This is the day when the people of our country have started claiming the country back. This is a victory for the youth of India. They have done it in the way Mahatma Gandhi had taught us.”
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge described Mr. Pradhan’s resignation as a defeat of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s “stubbornness”. He added that the PM should apologise and take strict action against all those who used force against the agitating students.
Congress General Secretary (organisation) K. C. Venugopal said the Opposition had been spearheading the protest in a united fashion, while party general secretary (communication) Jairam Ramesh said the Opposition had demonstrated “rock-solid unity and solidarity” with the students.
Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said the resignation was a major victory for the new generation. “The government had to bow down,” he said.
Education reforms sought
Speaking to the media in Uttar Pradesh, Mr. Yadav said the movement had underlined the need for serious reforms in the education sector, from primary schooling to higher education.
Aam Aadmi Party supremo and former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal said Mr. Pradhan’s resignation was a “big win for democracy”.
The Left parties also welcomed the resignation and demanded a comprehensive reform in the education sector.
CPI General Secretary D Raja said the resignation was a rare moment of democratic accountability. “It is a rare moment of democratic accountability, achieved not through the goodwill of an arrogant government, but through the sustained struggle of students and youth across the country. The students’ movement has defeated the arrogance of the BJP and compelled the Modi-Shah regime to answer for its failures,” he said.
CPI(M) congratulated the students who were part of the protest and demanded, in a post on X, a comprehensive reform in the education sector, including the scrapping of the National Testing Agency (NTA) and the rollback of the National Education Policy (NEP).
“(Mr Pradhan’s) resignation is only the first step. Now the NTA has to be disbanded, and the anti-student, commercial and communal NEP 2020 has to be rolled back. Cases foisted on the protesters have to be dropped, and action has to be taken against all police personnel who brutally attacked our students,” CPI(M) General Secretary M A Baby said.
Deepankar Bhattacharya of the CPI(ML) said the resignation was “the only sensible thing” Mr. Pradhan had done. “The only sensible thing you have ever done, even though you have not shown the minimum courage and honesty to admit that your resignation has been ordered by the youth of India,” he said.

headline: NEW DELHI: Amid the ongoing student protest, Delhi police have deployed around 3,000 police personnel to maintain law and order for nearly 10,000 people present in and around Jantar Mantar.
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Amid the ongoing student protest, Delhi police have deployed around 3,000 police personnel to maintain law and order for nearly 10,000 people present in and around Jantar Mantar.
Police sources said around 130 police personnel have been injured and 15 FIRs have been registered in connection with the agitation, according to Delhi Police sources. The police also said around 65 students sustained injuries during the demonstrations.
The Delhi Police further said it is using Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras to identify "anti-social elements" visiting Jantar Mantar.
According to police sources, more than 2,000 people with criminal records who had visited the protest site have been identified so far, as cited by ANI.
This is not the first time the Delhi Police has deployed Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras.
The force has previously used the technology as part of security arrangements during Republic Day, Independence Day, Holi, Diwali, Eid, Ramlila celebrations and several other major public events across the city.
Meanwhile, Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday said he has been diagnosed with typhoid but asserted that the nationwide protests demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan would continue without interruption.
On Friday, Dipke welcomed activist Sonam Wangchuk's decision to end his 26-day hunger strike but reiterated that the movement would continue until its demand for accountability over the examination irregularities is met.
"Our demonstration will go on until Dharmendra Pradhan steps down. Any meeting must take place at a neutral location or venue. Nothing less than the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan will be accepted," he said.
Meanwhile, activist Sonam Wangchuk responded to criticism over his decision to end his 26-day hunger strike held in support of students protesting the alleged NEET paper leak.
In a video message shared on social media, Wangchuk questioned why his commitment to the cause required a "character certificate".
Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike after receiving a written assurance from the Union government on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.
The activist said he had earlier been offered verbal assurances but insisted on a written commitment, which delayed the end of his fast by two days.
Following a nearly two-hour meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, representatives of CJP said the government had sought time until Saturday afternoon to consider their demand for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
